questions.prompt: Do you prefer writing by hand or typing on a keyboard?
questions.sampleA2:
I like keyboard more.

Because it is fast.

And I can write emails.

But sometimes I write by hand.
questions.sampleB1:
I prefer typing on a keyboard. I think it's quicker.

Also, it's easier to correct mistakes on a computer.

However, I sometimes write by hand for notes.

For example, when I'm studying, I like to write things down.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm firmly in the typing camp for anything serious. The thing is, I can get my thoughts down so much faster, and editing is a breeze compared to scribbling and crossing things out. That said, I do jot down quick notes by hand now and then — there's something about it that helps ideas stick.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga klaviatura ko'proq yoqadi.

Chunki u tez.

Va men elektron pochta xatlarini yoza olaman.

Lekin ba'zida men qo'lda yozaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men klaviaturada yozishni afzal ko'raman. Menimcha, bu tezroq.

Shuningdek, kompyuterda xatolarni tuzatish osonroq.

Lekin, ba'zida qo'lda, eslatmalar uchun yozaman.

Masalan, o'qiyotganimda, narsalarni yozib olishni yoqtiraman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Umuman olganda, ko'pgina yozuv vazifalari uchun klaviaturada terishni afzal ko'raman.

Tezlik va samaradorlik shunchaki tengsiz, ayniqsa, uzunroq hujjatlar yoki tahrirlash va qayta ko'rib chiqishni talab qiladigan loyihalar bilan ishlashda.

Shunga qaramay, men ba'zi vaziyatlarda qo'lda yozishning taktil tajribasini qadrlayman.

Misol uchun, g'oyalarni muhokama qilish yoki dastlabki kontseptsiyalarni ishlab chiqishda, qo'lda yozish yanada organik tuyulishi va ijodiy oqimning katta tuyg'usiga imkon berishi mumkin.

Oxir-oqibat, eng yaxshi usul muayyan kontekstga va kutilgan natijaga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you prefer writing by hand or typing on a keyboard?
idioms: The pen is mightier than the sword - "Qalam qilichdan kuchli"
put pen to paper - "yozishga kirishmoq"
in black and white - "yozma ravishda, aniq"
sentenceStarters: "I honestly prefer typing on a keyboard for..." - "Men rostdan ham ... uchun klaviaturada yozishni afzal ko'raman"
"However, I do enjoy writing by hand when..." - "Biroq, men ... bo'lganda qo'lda yozishni yoqtiraman"
"I think both methods have their place..." - "Menimcha, ikkala usulning ham o'z o'rni bor..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I honestly prefer typing on a keyboard for most tasks. It's much faster and more convenient, especially when I need to write something long like an essay or a report.
However, I do enjoy writing by hand when it comes to personal things like greeting cards or journal entries. There's something uniquely satisfying about putting pen to paper — it feels more intimate and thoughtful.
I think both methods have their place. Typing is better for productivity and efficiency, while handwriting adds a personal touch that no digital font can replicate. As they say, "The pen is mightier than the sword".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men ko'p vazifalar uchun klaviaturada yozishni afzal ko'raman, to'g'risi. Bu ancha tezroq va qulayroq, ayniqsa, insho yoki hisobot kabi uzunroq narsa yozishim kerak bo'lganda.

Lekin, tabrik kartochkalari yoki kundalik yozuvlari kabi shaxsiy narsalarga kelganda, qo'lda yozish menga yoqadi. Qalamni qog'ozga qo'yishda o'zgacha qoniqish bor - u yanada samimiy va o'ychan tuyuladi.

O'ylaymanki, ikkala usulning ham o'z o'rni bor. Klaviaturada yozish unumdorlik va samaradorlik uchun yaxshiroq, qo'lda yozish esa hech qanday raqamli shrift takrorlay olmaydigan shaxsiy teginishni qo'shadi. Aytishlaricha, "Qalam qilichdan kuchliroq".

questions.prompt: How much water do you usually drink every day?
questions.sampleA1: I drink water. Maybe two glasses. I like water.
questions.sampleA2: I drink water every day. I think I drink four glasses. I drink water because it is good.
questions.sampleB1: I usually drink about six glasses of water a day. I try to drink more, but sometimes I forget. In my opinion, it's important to drink enough water. For example, it helps with my skin and energy levels.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, I try to drink around two litres a day, though I'll admit I don't always manage it. The thing is, I keep a bottle on my desk, so I end up sipping away without really thinking about it. When I've been to the gym, I obviously need to top up a fair bit more to stay properly hydrated.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men suv ichaman. Balki ikki stakan. Menga suv yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men har kuni suv ichaman. Menimcha, to'rt stakan ichaman. Men suv ichaman, chunki u foydali.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men odatda kuniga olti stakan suv ichaman. Ko'proq ichishga harakat qilaman, lekin ba'zida unutib qolaman. Mening fikrimcha, yetarli suv ichish muhim. Misol uchun, bu mening terim va energiya darajamga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men odatda kuniga taxminan ikki litr suv ichaman deb ayta olaman, garchi bu ob-havo va faollik darajamga qarab o'zgaradi. Kun davomida ichishni eslatib turish uchun o'zim bilan suv idishini olib yurishga harakat qilaman. To'g'ri gidratatsiyaning ahamiyatini kam baholash oson, lekin men bu mening energiya darajam va umumiy farovonligimga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatishini sezdim. Menimcha, yetarli miqdorda suv ichish - yaxshi sog'liqni saqlashning oddiy, ammo samarali usuli.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - How much water do you usually drink every day?
idioms: Water is the driving force of all nature - "Suv butun tabiatning harakatlantiruvchi kuchi"
water under the bridge - "o'tgan ish o'tgan"
still waters run deep - "tinch suv chuqur oqadi"
sentenceStarters: "I try to drink at least approximately..." - "Men har kuni kamida taxminan ... ichishga harakat qilaman"
"I usually start my morning with..." - "Men odatda tongimni ... bilan boshlayman"
"I think many people unfortunately don't drink enough..." - "Menimcha, ko'p odamlar afsuski yetarli ... ichmaydi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I try to drink at least approximately two litres of water every day, which is about eight glasses. I've made it a conscious habit to stay hydrated throughout the day.
I usually start my morning with a large glass of water, and I keep a water bottle on my desk so I can sip regularly. During the summer months, I naturally drink more because of the heat.
I think many people unfortunately don't drink enough water and underestimate its importance for overall health. Staying properly hydrated helps with concentration, energy levels, and even skin health. As they say, "Water is the driving force of all nature".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men har kuni kamida taxminan ikki litr suv ichishga harakat qilaman, bu taxminan sakkiz stakanga teng. Men kun davomida yetarlicha suv ichib turishni ongli odatga aylantirdim.

Men odatda ertalabni katta bir stakan suv bilan boshlayman va stolimda suv idishini saqlayman, shunda men muntazam ravishda suv ichib tura olaman. Yoz oylarida issiq tufayli men tabiiy ravishda ko'proq suv ichaman.

Menimcha, ko'p odamlar afsuski yetarli suv ichmaydilar va uning umumiy salomatlik uchun ahamiyatini kam baholaydilar. Yetarlicha suv ichish diqqatni jamlashga, energiya darajasiga va hatto teri salomatligiga yordam beradi. Aytishlaricha, "Suv - butun tabiatning harakatlantiruvchi kuchidir".

questions.prompt: What is your favorite public holiday in your country?
questions.sampleA2:
My favorite holiday is New Year.

It is in January.

I like it because I get presents and I see my family.

We eat a lot of food.
questions.sampleB1:
My favorite public holiday is probably Independence Day.

It's in July, and we celebrate our country's freedom.

I think it's a good holiday because everyone gets together and has barbecues.

Also, there are fireworks, which are really fun to watch.

However, it can be very crowded everywhere.
questions.sampleB2: My favourite has to be Navruz, hands down. It marks the arrival of spring, and the whole country comes alive with it. Families get together, cook a special dish called sumalak, and there's this real sense of a fresh start. To be honest, what I love most is how it brings everyone together, regardless of background.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Mening eng sevimli bayramim Yangi yil.

U yanvar oyida bo'ladi.

Menga u yoqadi, chunki men sovg'alar olaman va oilamni ko'raman.

Biz ko'p ovqat yeymiz.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Mening eng sevimli davlat bayramim, ehtimol, Mustaqillik kuni.

U iyulda bo'lib o'tadi va biz mamlakatimizning ozodligini nishonlaymiz.

Menimcha, bu yaxshi bayram, chunki hamma birga yig'ilib, barbekyu qiladi.

Shuningdek, otashinlar bo'ladi, ularni tomosha qilish juda qiziqarli.

Ammo, hamma joyda juda gavjum bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men aytishim kerakki, mening eng sevimli davlat bayramim – Minnatdorchilik kuni.

Garchi u
asosan Shimoliy Amerikada nishonlansa ham, minnatdorchilikni ifoda etishning asosiy tushunchasi menga juda yoqadi.

Bu – oilalar birga yig'iladigan, ko'pincha uzoq masofalarga sayohat qilib, ovqatni baham ko'radigan va minnatdor bo'lgan narsalari haqida o'ylaydigan vaqt.

Haddan tashqari tijoratlashtirilgan ba'zi bayramlardan farqli o'laroq, Minnatdorchilik kuni hali ham oila va jamiyatga kuchli e'tibor qaratadi.

Albatta, taomlar asosiy diqqatga sazovor, lekin bundan tashqari, yaqinlar bilan qayta bog'lanish va hayotning oddiy narsalarini qadrlash imkoniyati uni juda ham maxsus qiladi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What is your favorite public holiday in your country?
idioms: Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end - "Har bir yangi boshlanish boshqa boshlanishning tugashidan keladi"
ring in the New Year - "Yangi yilni nishonlamoq"
out with the old, in with the new - "eskini tashlab, yangini qabul qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "My favourite public holiday is definitely..." - "Mening sevimli davlat bayramim, albatta..."
"What I love most about it is the sense of..." - "Men unda eng yoqtiradigan narsa ... hissi"
"It's also a time when people..." - "Bu shuningdek odamlar ... vaqt"

questions.sampleAnswer:
My favourite public holiday is definitely Navruz, which we celebrate on the 21st of March every year. It marks the beginning of spring and the New Year in our culture.
What I love most about Navruz is the sense of togetherness and renewal it brings. Families gather to prepare traditional dishes like sumalak, which takes an entire night to cook. The streets are filled with music, dancing, and incredibly festive energy.
It's also a time when people forgive past disagreements and start fresh. I think that's a beautiful tradition. As they say, "Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng sevimli davlat bayramim, albatta, har yili 21-martda nishonlanadigan Navro'z. U bahorning boshlanishini va bizning madaniyatimizda Yangi yilni anglatadi.

Navro'zning menga eng yoqadigan jihati - bu olib keladigan birlik va yangilanish hissi. Oilalar sumalak kabi an'anaviy taomlarni tayyorlash uchun yig'ilishadi, uni pishirish uchun butun tun kerak bo'ladi. Ko'chalar musiqa, raqs va nihoyatda bayramona energiya bilan to'la.

Bu, shuningdek, odamlar o'tmishdagi kelishmovchiliklarni kechiradigan va yangidan boshlaydigan vaqt. Menimcha, bu juda go'zal an'ana. Aytishlaricha, "Har bir yangi boshlanish, boshqa bir boshlanishning oxiridan kelib chiqadi".

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see snow.

I see sun.

Cold and hot.
questions.sampleA2:
I see a person in the snow.

And I see a person in the sun.

The snow is cold but the sun is hot.
questions.sampleB1:
In the first picture, I see someone with a coat because it's cold.

In the second picture, I see someone with sunglasses because it's sunny.

I think the weather is very different in the two pictures.

For example, one is winter and the other is summer.
questions.sampleB2:
The first picture depicts a scene of a snowy city street, likely during winter. Several people are out and about, bundled up in warm clothing as heavy snow falls. In the foreground, two young women are walking and eating something, perhaps to keep warm. It gives a sense of daily life continuing despite the challenging weather.

By contrast, the second image shows a family of four enjoying themselves by a swimming pool in a sunny, tropical location. They are lounging on sunbeds, looking relaxed and happy, with palm trees visible in the background. While the first picture portrays the harsh realities of winter, the second evokes a feeling of warmth, leisure, and a much-needed break.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men qor ko'ryapman.

Men quyosh ko'ryapman.

Sovuq va issiq.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men qorda bir odamni ko'ryapman.

Va men quyoshda bir odamni ko'ryapman.

Qor sovuq, lekin quyosh issiq.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda men palto kiygan odamni ko'ryapman, chunki havo sovuq.

Ikkinchi rasmda men quyoshdan ko'zoynak taqqan odamni ko'ryapman, chunki havo quyoshli.

Menimcha, ikkala rasmdagi ob-havo juda farqli.

Masalan, biri qish, ikkinchisi esa yoz.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda qishda odam tasvirlangan, ehtimol juda sovuq joyda, chunki u kiygan kiyimlar sonidan shunday xulosa qilish mumkin.

Ikkinchi rasm esa, aksincha, quyoshli kundan zavqlanayotgan odamni ko'rsatadi, ehtimol iliq iqlimda.

Bu ikki qarama-qarshi rasmni yonma-yon ko'rish juda qiziq, chunki ular odamlarning yashash joyiga va yilning vaqtiga qarab turli xil tajribalarga ega ekanligini ta'kidlaydi.

Rasmlar ob-havo sharoitlarining haddan tashqari holatlarini juda yaxshi ko'rsatib beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: as different as night and day - "tundan kunduzgacha farq"
under the weather - "kasal bo'lmoq"
every cloud has a silver lining - "har qanday qiyinchilikda ham yaxshi tomon bor"
sentenceStarters: "These two pictures show people living in..." - "Bu ikki rasm ... da yashaydigan odamlarni ko'rsatadi"
"In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman"
"The second picture presents a completely opposite scene..." - "Ikkinchi rasm butunlay qarama-qarshi manzarani ko'rsatadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures show people living in completely different climate conditions.
In the first picture, I can see a person bundled up in heavy winter clothes, walking down a snow-covered street. The weather looks extremely cold, and the person is wearing thick layers, a scarf, and probably gloves to protect themselves from the freezing temperatures.
The second picture presents a completely opposite scene — a person in light summer clothing, wearing sunglasses and clearly enjoying a hot, sunny day. They look relaxed and comfortable in the warm weather. The contrast between these two images perfectly illustrates how different life can be depending on the climate you live in.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasmda butunlay boshqa iqlim sharoitlarida yashayotgan odamlar ko'rsatilgan.

Birinchi rasmda men qalin qishki kiyimga o'ralgan, qor bilan qoplangan ko'chada ketayotgan odamni ko'rishim mumkin. Ob-havo juda sovuq ko'rinadi va odam muzlash haroratidan himoyalanish uchun qalin qatlamlar, sharf va ehtimol qo'lqop kiygan.

Ikkinchi rasmda butunlay qarama-qarshi manzara namoyon bo'ladi — yengil yozgi kiyimdagi, quyoshdan saqlaydigan ko'zoynak taqqan va aniq issiq, quyoshli kundan zavqlanayotgan odam. Ular issiq ob-havoda xotirjam va qulay ko'rinadi. Bu ikki rasm o'rtasidagi farq siz yashayotgan iqlimga qarab hayot qanchalik farq qilishi mumkinligini mukammal tarzda ko'rsatib beradi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of living in a place with a cold, snowy climate?
questions.sampleA1: Snow is nice. I like snow. Cold is okay.
questions.sampleA2: I like snow. It is pretty. And I can make a snowman. But it is very cold and I don't like cold.
questions.sampleB1: I think living in a cold place is good sometimes. For example, you can go skiing which is fun. Also, the snow looks very beautiful. However, it can be difficult to go outside when it's very cold. I think it's better to have both warm and cold weather.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose the biggest draw is the sheer beauty of it — a blanket of snow makes everything look magical. On top of that, you can throw yourself into winter sports like skiing and snowboarding, which are great fun. The cold also tends to keep pests at bay, so there are fewer insects to put up with. All in all, it has its perks.
questions.uzSampleA1: Qor yaxshi. Menga qor yoqadi. Sovuq ham yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga qor yoqadi. U chiroyli. Va men qorbobo yasay olaman. Lekin juda sovuq va men sovuqni yoqtirmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, sovuq joyda yashash ba'zan yaxshi. Masalan, chang'ida uchish mumkin, bu juda qiziqarli. Yana, qor juda chiroyli ko'rinadi. Biroq, juda sovuq bo'lganda tashqariga chiqish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Menimcha, iliq va sovuq ob-havo birgalikda bo'lgani yaxshiroq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, bir afzalligi, albatta, manzaradir. Qor bilan qoplangan landshaft juda chiroyli va sokin bo'lishi mumkin. Shuningdek, chang'i va snoubord kabi qishki sport turlari bilan shug'ullanish imkoniyati mavjud, ular ajoyib mashq va qiziqarli. Menimcha, yana bir foydasi shundaki, sovuq haroratlar ba'zi hasharotlarni o'ldirishga moyil, ya'ni hal qilish kerak bo'lgan kamroq hasharotlar bo'ladi. Biroq, sovuq ba'zi odamlar uchun juda izolyatsiya qiluvchi va qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of living in a place with a cold, snowy climate?
idioms: There's no such thing as bad weather, only bad clothing - "Yomon ob-havo yo'q, faqat yomon kiyim bor"
break the ice - "muzni sindirmoq, suhbat boshlamoq"
tip of the iceberg - "muzlikning uchi"
sentenceStarters: "Living in a cold, snowy climate has several notable advantages..." - "Sovuq, qorli iqlimda yashashning bir nechta e'tiborga molik afzalliklari bor..."
"Firstly, cold climates offer stunning natural beauty..." - "Birinchidan, sovuq iqlim ajoyib tabiiy go'zallikni taqdim etadi..."
"Additionally, research suggests that people in colder regions..." - "Bundan tashqari, tadqiqotlar sovuqroq hududlardagi odamlar ... ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Living in a cold, snowy climate, as depicted in the first picture, has several notable advantages that many people appreciate.
Firstly, cold climates offer stunning natural beauty. There's something truly magical about waking up to a world covered in fresh white snow. The changing seasons also bring a wonderful variety to life — from snowy winters to colourful springs.
Secondly, cold weather provides opportunities for unique recreational activities like skiing, snowboarding, ice skating, and building snowmen. These are experiences that people in tropical climates simply cannot enjoy.
Additionally, research suggests that people in colder regions tend to develop a stronger sense of community — harsh winters encourage people to help each other and spend quality time indoors with family and friends. Cold weather also means fewer insects and certain diseases are less common. As they say, "There's no such thing as bad weather, only bad clothing".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Sovuq, qorli iqlimda yashash, birinchi rasmdagi kabi, ko'pchilik qadrlaydigan bir nechta sezilarli afzalliklarga ega.

Birinchidan, sovuq iqlimlar hayratlanarli tabiiy go'zallikni taklif etadi. Yangi oq qor bilan qoplangan dunyoga uyg'onishda chindan ham sehrli narsa bor. Yilning fasllari almashinuvi ham hayotga ajoyib xilma-xillik olib keladi - qorli qishlardan rang-barang bahorlargacha.

Ikkinchidan, sovuq ob-havo chang'i uchish, snoubord, konkida uchish va qor odam yasash kabi noyob dam olish tadbirlari uchun imkoniyatlar yaratadi. Bu tropik iqlimdagi odamlar oddiygina bahramand bo'la olmaydigan tajribalar.

Bundan tashqari, tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, sovuqroq hududlardagi odamlar kuchliroq jamoatchilik tuyg'usini rivojlantirishga moyil - qattiq qishlar odamlarni bir-biriga yordam berishga va oila va do'stlar bilan uyda sifatli vaqt o'tkazishga undaydi. Sovuq ob-havo, shuningdek, kamroq hasharotlar va ba'zi kasalliklar kamroq tarqalganligini anglatadi. Aytishlaricha, "Yomon ob-havo degan narsa yo'q, faqat yomon kiyim bor".

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer to live in regions with hot weather all year round?
questions.sampleA1: I like hot weather. The sun is good. I like swimming. Hot is good.
questions.sampleA2: I like hot weather because I can go to the beach. And I don't like cold weather because it's sad. My friend likes hot weather too, but my mother likes the winter.
questions.sampleB1: Some people like hot weather all the time. I think it's because they like being outside. For example, they can swim and play sports. Also, it might be cheaper because they don't need to pay for heating. However, I prefer some cold weather too.
questions.sampleB2: Well, off the top of my head, I'd say it comes down to lifestyle. In a warm climate, you can spend loads of time outdoors — swimming, hiking, that sort of thing — without the seasons getting in the way. On top of that, people tend to be more sociable when the sun's out. And let's face it, the heating bills are a lot lower.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga issiq ob-havo yoqadi. Quyosh yaxshi. Suzishni yoqtiraman. Issiq yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga issiq ob-havo yoqadi, chunki men plyajga borishim mumkin. Va sovuq ob-havo yoqtirmayman, chunki u qayg'uli. Mening do'stimga ham issiq ob-havo yoqadi, lekin onamga qish yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ba'zi odamlarga doim issiq ob-havo yoqadi. Menimcha, buning sababi ularga tashqarida bo'lish yoqadi.
Masalan, ular suzishlari va sport bilan shug'ullanishlari mumkin. Shuningdek, isitish uchun pul to'lashga hojat yo'qligi sababli, bu arzonroq bo'lishi mumkin.
Biroq, men sovuq ob-havoni ham afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, menimcha, kimdir doimiy issiq ob-havoni afzal ko'rishining bir nechta sabablari bor. Birinchidan, bu ma'lum bir turmush tarzini ta'minlaydi - yil fasllari o'zgarishi haqida qayg'urmasdan, ko'proq vaqtni ochiq havoda, suzish yoki piyoda sayr qilish kabi mashg'ulotlar bilan o'tkazish imkonini beradi. Ikkinchidan, issiqroq iqlim odamlarni tabiiy ravishda ochiq joylarga jalb qilgani sababli, ijtimoiy munosabatlar uchun qulayroq, deb ta'kidlash mumkin. Nihoyat, isitish uchun to'lovlarining pastligi, ayniqsa energiya narxlari oshib borayotganini hisobga olsak, albatta, afzallikdir.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some people prefer to live in regions with hot weather all year round?
idioms: Where there is sunshine, there is hope - "Quyosh nur sochgan joyda umid bor"
make hay while the sun shines - "imkoniyatdan foydalanmoq"
a place in the sun - "qulay o'rin, baxtli hayot"
phrases: active outdoor lifestyle - "faol ochiq havoda hayot tarzi"
positive effect on mental health - "ruhiy salomatlikka ijobiy ta'sir"
sentenceStarters: "Many people are drawn to living in hot climates..." - "Ko'p odamlarni issiq iqlimda yashash jalb qiladi..."
"Primarily, warm weather allows for a more..." - "Birinchi navbatda, iliq ob-havo ko'proq ... imkonini beradi"
"Moreover, many studies suggest that sunshine has a..." - "Bundan tashqari, ko'plab tadqiqotlar quyosh nuri ... ta'sir ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many people are drawn to living in hot climates year-round, as we can see the person enjoying in the second picture, and there are several understandable reasons for this preference.
Primarily, warm weather allows for a more active outdoor lifestyle. People can go to the beach, swim, jog, and socialise outdoors at any time of year without worrying about snowstorms or icy roads. This naturally leads to a more relaxed and enjoyable daily routine.
Furthermore, living in a warm climate can be significantly cheaper in terms of heating costs. In cold regions, energy bills during winter can be enormous, whereas in warm areas, people spend far less on keeping their homes comfortable.
Moreover, many studies suggest that sunshine has a positive effect on mental health. Sunlight boosts vitamin D levels and helps prevent seasonal depression, which is common in colder, darker climates. People in sunny places often report feeling happier and more energetic. As they say, "Where there is sunshine, there is hope".

Ko'pchilik yil davomida issiq iqlimda yashashga intiladi, buni ikkinchi rasmda odamning zavqlanayotganini ko'rishimiz mumkin va bu afzallik uchun bir nechta tushunarli sabablar bor.

Avvalo, iliq ob-havo ko'proq faol ochiq havoda hayot tarzini olib borishga imkon beradi. Odamlar plyajga borishlari, suzishlari, yugurishlari va yilning istalgan vaqtida qor bo'ronlari yoki muzli yo'llar haqida tashvishlanmasdan ochiq havoda muloqot qilishlari mumkin. Bu, tabiiyki, yanada xotirjam va yoqimli kundalik tartibga olib keladi.

Bundan tashqari, issiq iqlimda yashash isitish xarajatlari nuqtai nazaridan ancha arzon bo'lishi mumkin. Sovuq hududlarda qish davrida energiya to'lovlari juda katta bo'lishi mumkin, issiq hududlarda esa odamlar o'z uylarini qulay saqlash uchun ancha kam xarajat qiladilar.

Bundan tashqari, ko'plab tadqiqotlar quyosh nurining ruhiy salomatlikka ijobiy ta'siri borligini ko'rsatadi. Quyosh nuri D vitamini darajasini oshiradi va sovuq, qorong'i iqlimda keng tarqalgan mavsumiy depressiyaning oldini olishga yordam beradi. Quyoshli joylarda odamlar ko'pincha o'zlarini baxtliroq va tetikroq his qilishlarini aytishadi. Aytishlaricha, "Quyosh bor joyda umid bor".

I think it was quite successful because everyone enjoyed the food and the music. However, the weather wasn't great, so we had to move inside later.
questions.sampleB2: Right, let me tell you about a surprise birthday party I put together for my best friend last year — her thirtieth, which felt like a big milestone, so I really wanted to pull out all the stops. To be honest, organising it was no walk in the park. The first hurdle was keeping it under wraps, because she's incredibly sharp and picks up on the smallest thing. I had to come up with a cover story about a quiet dinner, just the two of us, so she wouldn't suspect a thing. Behind the scenes, I was rushed off my feet. I booked a private room at a restaurant she loves, roped in around twenty of her closest friends, and sorted out the decorations, a cake, and a playlist of songs I knew she'd adore. The thing that took the most effort was coordinating everyone's arrival — I sent out a group message telling them to turn up half an hour early and lie low until she walked in. When the big moment came, everyone jumped out and shouted 'surprise', and honestly, the look on her face was priceless. She was completely taken aback, and even welled up a little, which set everyone off. The evening went off without a hitch — the food was spot on, people mingled, and we danced well into the night. Looking back, all the stress was absolutely worth it. Seeing her that happy made me realise there's nothing quite like pulling off a surprise for someone you care about.

bulletPoints: Describe an event or party that you organized.
How did organizing this event influence your planning and time-management skills?
What role do celebrations and events play in bringing communities together?
questions.sampleAnswer:
An event I organized:
Last year, I organized a surprise birthday party for my younger brother's 18th birthday. It was the first major event I had ever planned entirely on my own, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable experiences for our whole family. I booked a small café, arranged decorations, ordered a custom cake, and secretly invited about 30 of his closest friends. The surprise on his face when he walked in was absolutely priceless.
How it influenced my planning and time-management skills:
Organizing this event significantly improved my planning abilities. I had to create a detailed timeline, manage a budget, coordinate with different vendors, and make sure everything came together at the right moment. I learned to prioritise tasks, delegate responsibilities to friends who offered to help, and always have a backup plan. It taught me that good time management is about working smart, not just working hard.
The role of celebrations in bringing communities together:
I firmly believe that celebrations and events play a vital role in building community bonds. They give people a reason to come together, share joy, and create lasting memories. Whether it's a wedding, a national holiday, or a neighbourhood festival, these gatherings strengthen social ties and remind us of what we have in common. As they say, "We don't remember days, we remember moments".

Men tashkil qilgan tadbir:

O'tgan yili men ukamning 18 yoshga to'lgan kuniga bag'ishlab, unga syurpriz tug'ilgan kun kechasi tashkil qildim. Bu men birinchi marta butunlay o'zim rejalashtirgan yirik tadbir edi va u butun oilamiz uchun eng unutilmas voqealardan biriga aylandi. Men kichik bir kafeni bron qildim, bezaklarni tashkillashtirdim, maxsus tortga buyurtma berdim va uning eng yaqin 30 ga yaqin do'stlarini yashirincha taklif qildim. U kirganida uning yuzidagi hayrat mutlaqo bebaho edi.

Bu mening rejalashtirish va vaqtni boshqarish qobiliyatlarimga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Ushbu tadbirni tashkil qilish mening rejalashtirish qobiliyatlarimni sezilarli darajada yaxshiladi. Men batafsil vaqt jadvalini tuzishim, byudjetni boshqarishim, turli yetkazib beruvchilar bilan muvofiqlashtirishim va hamma narsa to'g'ri vaqtda birlashishiga ishonch hosil qilishim kerak edi. Men vazifalarni ustuvorlashtirishni, yordam berishni taklif qilgan do'stlarga mas'uliyatni topshirishni va har doim zaxira rejasiga ega bo'lishni o'rgandim. Bu menga yaxshi vaqtni boshqarish shunchaki qattiq ishlash emas, balki aqlli ishlash ekanligini o'rgatdi.

Jamiyatlarni birlashtirishda bayramlarning roli:

Men bayramlar va tadbirlar jamiyat aloqalarini mustahkamlashda muhim rol o'ynashiga qat'iy ishonaman. Ular odamlarga birga yig'ilish, quvonchni baham ko'rish va uzoq muddatli xotiralarni yaratish uchun sabab beradi. To'y, milliy bayram yoki mahalliy festival bo'ladimi, bu yig'ilishlar ijtimoiy aloqalarni mustahkamlaydi va bizga umumiy jihatlarimizni eslatadi. Aytishlaricha, "Biz kunlarni emas, lahzalarni eslaymiz".

questions.sampleB2: This is a really thorny issue, and to be honest, I can see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, there's a strong case for banning it outright. Young children simply don't have the critical thinking skills to see through advertising — they take everything at face value. Clever marketing can nudge them towards junk food, sugary cereals and the latest must-have toy, which piles pressure on parents and can fuel unhealthy habits down the line. In that sense, kids are a soft target, and it feels a bit unfair to exploit that. On the other hand, a blanket ban strikes me as going too far. For one thing, it could be seen as an infringement on free speech, and businesses would argue they have every right to promote their products. What's more, not all advertising is harmful — some of it points children towards books, educational games or healthy snacks. Enforcing a total ban would also be a nightmare in practice, given how much content kids consume online these days. So where do I stand? On balance, I'd steer clear of an outright ban and push for much tighter regulation instead. I reckon we should crack down on junk-food ads during children's programmes and set clear limits on what companies can and can't do. At the end of the day, it's about striking a balance between protecting kids and respecting freedom of expression. A sensible middle ground would serve everyone far better than a heavy-handed ban.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly contentious issue that affects families and businesses across the globe.
Those in favour of banning advertising targeted at children make several persuasive arguments. Firstly, young children lack the critical thinking skills to distinguish between entertainment and marketing. They are easily manipulated by colourful ads and catchy jingles without understanding the commercial intent behind them. Secondly, much of children's advertising promotes unhealthy habits — sugary cereals, fast food, and fizzy drinks are among the most heavily advertised products to kids. Furthermore, this advertising creates significant financial pressure on parents, as children constantly demand the latest toys and gadgets they've seen on screen.
However, opponents raise important counterpoints. Some advertisements can actually be educational, informing both parents and children about useful or innovative products. Moreover, advertising revenue is what funds many free children's programmes and educational apps — without it, these resources might disappear or become expensive. Additionally, many argue that it is ultimately the parents' responsibility to teach their children about money and consumerism, rather than relying on government bans.
Personally, I believe we need stricter regulations rather than an outright ban. Children deserve protection, but advertising can be done responsibly. As they say, "With great power comes great responsibility".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu oilalar va bizneslarga butun dunyo bo'ylab ta'sir qiladigan juda bahsli masala.

Bolalarga qaratilgan reklamalarni taqiqlash tarafdorlari bir nechta ishonarli dalillarni keltiradilar. Birinchidan, yosh bolalarda ko'ngilochar va marketing o'rtasidagi farqni ajratish uchun tanqidiy fikrlash qobiliyati yetishmaydi. Ular rang-barang reklamalar va esda qolarli qo'shiqlardan ularning orqasidagi tijorat maqsadini tushunmasdan osonlikcha manipulyatsiya qilinadi. Ikkinchidan, bolalar reklamalarining aksariyati nosog'lom odatlarni targ'ib qiladi — shakarli donlar, tez tayyorlanadigan ovqatlar va gazli ichimliklar bolalarga eng ko'p reklama qilinadigan mahsulotlar qatoriga kiradi. Bundan tashqari, bu reklama ota-onalarga katta moliyaviy bosim o'tkazadi, chunki bolalar doimo ekranda ko'rgan eng so'nggi o'yinchoqlar va gadjetlarni talab qiladilar.

Biroq, qarshilar muhim qarshi fikrlarni ilgari suradilar. Ba'zi reklamalar aslida ota-onalar va bolalarni foydali yoki innovatsion mahsulotlar haqida xabardor qilib, ta'lim berishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, reklama daromadi ko'plab bepul bolalar dasturlari va ta'limiy ilovalarni moliyalashtiradi — usiz bu resurslar yo'qolishi yoki qimmatga tushishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilikning ta'kidlashicha, bu hukumat taqiqlashiga tayanishdan ko'ra, pul va iste'molchilik haqida bolalarga o'rgatish ota-onalarning mas'uliyati hisoblanadi.

Shaxsan men, to'liq taqiqlashdan ko'ra, qat'iyroq qoidalarga muhtojmiz, deb hisoblayman. Bolalar himoyaga loyiq, lekin reklamani mas'uliyat bilan amalga oshirish mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Katta kuch bilan katta mas'uliyat keladi".
